sentences.text:
This bail application has been filed by the applicant-accused in case crime No.308 of 2023, under
Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and section 3/4 D.P. Act, police station Kadadham, District Kaushambi
with the prayer to enlarge the applicant-accused on bail.

entities.text: D.P. Act, police station Kadadham, District Kaushambi
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3.  It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is husband of deceased and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
The marriage of deceased with applicant has taken place in the year 2020.
Only general allegations of dowry demand and harassment of deceased have been levelled against all the accused persons including applicant.
Before incident, no complaint was made against the applicant during four years of marriage.

It was stated that incident took place during Ranu Raidas vs State Of U.P. on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99316921/
1 lock down period and merely some hot talk had taken place and deceased committed suicide.

entities.text: Ranu Raidas vs State Of U.P. on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In postmortem report except ligature mark, no injury has been shown on the body of the deceased and cause of death has been shown asphyxia as a result of ante-mortem hanging.
It is further stated that the applicant is languishing in jail since 24.11.2023 and even charges have not been framed so far and thus trial of the case would take sufficient time.
The applicant has no criminal history.
It was submitted that in case the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in trial.
4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the applicant is husband of deceased and deceased has suffered death due to hanging within seven years of marriage.

5. Considering submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the matter, a case for bail is made out.
6. The bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Ranu Raidas involved in aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing each a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:
i.
The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
ii. The applicant shall not pressurize/ intimidate any of the prosecution witness.

iii. 
The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless his / her personal presence is exempted.
iv. The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

8. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
9.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the Court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel bail of applicant in accordance with law.

Order Date :- 5.2.2025 Jitendra  Ranu Raidas vs State Of U.P. on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99316921/
